headline: Democrats win US midterms, Trump reshuffles his White House team, and the ASX dips as your US-exposed ETFs feel the pinch — but the long-term story stays intact.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS tracks the entire US share market, so it moves with the AUD/USD exchange rate as well as US stocks. The Aussie dollar fell today (down ~0.9% against the USD), which typically lifts VTS in AUD terms — but selling in US equities linked to AI regulation fears more than offset that, pushing VTS down 2.67% for the session.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: News that the Democrats — who now control Congress — plan a wave of AI regulation bills spooked investors in AI-focused stocks. This ETF holds the big AI names, so it copped a direct hit, falling 2.71% today. It's down 20% overall from your entry price, which is painful, but the long-term AI growth thesis hasn't collapsed — this is regulatory risk being priced in.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG is a diversified fund with heavy exposure to global (especially US) equities, so it followed the broader market lower today. The ASX slipped 0.49% and global sentiment was cautious post-midterms. No stock-specific issue — just broad market drag.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF, like VDHG, holds a broad mix of global shares and dipped 1.51% today in sympathy with the softer ASX and global equities. Nothing company-specific — it's riding the same wave as the wider market.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE bucked the trend today, rising 1.19%. Emerging markets often get a boost when the US dollar outlook softens or when investors rotate away from US tech. The post-midterm environment may be encouraging some money to flow into emerging market assets as a diversifier.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara was flat today at $2.83. Albemarle (a major US lithium producer) reported Q3 earnings overnight with a focus on cost discipline — suggesting the lithium market remains soft. PLS continues to trade well below your average entry price, reflecting the ongoing lithium price slump.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up 0.71% last night. Good news in the background: a former Rockstar tech director flagged that GTA 6's PC release could come sooner than expected to get ahead of AI-generated copycat versions. Take-Two also confirmed GTA Online will keep running when GTA 6 launches — both bits of news are positive for the long-term revenue story.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet gained 0.78% last night, holding up well despite broader tech wobbles. Analyst commentary from Seeking Alpha is bullish, calling it a 'strong buy', and Motley Fool analysis suggests Google's core search business remains solid despite surface-level concerns. The AI regulation fears hit some peers harder than Google.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 0.99% last night, caught up in the broader sell-off in AI and tech stocks as investors worried about what Democrat-led AI regulation could mean for big tech. The long-term position is still up nearly 20% overall, so this is a minor pullback in an otherwise strong holding.

watch_today.title: AI regulation fears hit your tech holdings
watch_today.detail: Democrats winning control of Congress last night triggered a wave of concern about incoming AI regulation bills. This directly hit GXAI.AX (down 2.71% today), VTS.AX (down 2.67%) and MSFT (down 0.99% last night). For a long-term holder, this is noise — the AI growth story is a decade-long trend, not a quarter. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX dip — long-term US market story unchanged
watch_today.detail: VTS fell 2.67% today, its biggest single-session drop in the portfolio. The cause is a mix of AI regulation jitters and a weaker broader market, not any fundamental problem with the US economy. As a long-term buy-and-hold investor, this kind of dip is exactly the sort of thing to ride through — the US total market has recovered from far worse.

watch_today.title: MSFT: down last night, still up 20% overall — hold firm
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped about 1% last night on AI regulation fears, but your position is still showing a solid 19.75% gain overall. Nothing structural has changed — Microsoft's AI products (Copilot, Azure AI) are real and generating revenue. This is a wobble, not a warning sign.

watch_today.title: RBA lifts cash rate to 4.85% — mortgage pain, but savings rates rising
watch_today.detail: The RBA has raised the official cash rate to 4.85%, with CBA, NAB, Westpac and ANZ all responding with savings account rate increases. If you have a mortgage, expect higher repayments. On the flip side, savings and term deposit rates are climbing. Watch how this affects consumer spending — it feeds through to ASX-listed companies.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium slump continues, hold for the long game
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is flat today but remains down 58% from your entry price. Albemarle's Q3 earnings (the world's biggest lithium producer) highlighted ongoing cost discipline — a sign the lithium market is still soft. There's no quick fix here, but if you believe in the long-term EV and battery storage story, the thesis hasn't changed. Only consider exiting if you no longer believe lithium demand will recover.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 PC release could come sooner — positive catalyst
watch_today.detail: A former Rockstar tech director has suggested GTA 6 could hit PC sooner than planned to beat AI-generated copycat versions flooding the market. Take-Two also confirmed GTA Online continues after GTA 6 launches, keeping that revenue stream alive. Both are good signs for the long-term investment case. Up 0.71% last night.

world.summary: The US midterms have flipped Congress to the Democrats, triggering a White House reshuffle, fresh debate over AI regulation, and ongoing military action in Iran. Ship attacks in the Persian Gulf are keeping oil prices elevated.

stories.title: Democrats win US midterms, handing Trump a major political blow
stories.why_it_matters: The Democrats have won back control of the US Congress in this week's midterm elections, a major setback for Donald Trump two years into his second term. The result opens the door for legislative pushback on Trump's agenda — including potential brakes on the Middle East conflict — and signals growing voter discontent. For Australia, it's a reminder that political winds can shift fast: commentators are already drawing comparisons to the challenges facing PM Albanese.

stories.title: Trump names Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff after midterm defeat
stories.why_it_matters: Trump has replaced Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff with Stephen Miller — the hardline architect of Trump's immigration crackdowns during his first term. Miller is known as one of the most ideologically driven figures in Trump's orbit, and his elevation signals Trump is doubling down on his base rather than pivoting to the centre after the midterm loss. Marco Rubio is also reportedly pushing back on resignation rumours, suggesting instability at the top of the administration.

stories.title: US launches new strikes on Iranian island as Tehran considers ceasefire proposals
stories.why_it_matters: The US has launched fresh military strikes on a key Iranian island even as Iran is reportedly weighing ceasefire proposals being mediated by Qatar. The situation is in a delicate phase — fighting continues while diplomacy is quietly underway. Qatar says mediation efforts remain on track. This conflict matters for your portfolio because any escalation near the Strait of Hormuz (the world's most important oil shipping lane) could spike oil prices and rattle global markets.

stories.title: Ships attacked in Persian Gulf, oil prices edge higher
stories.why_it_matters: More ships have been attacked in the Persian Gulf as the Iran conflict continues to spill into commercial shipping lanes. Oil prices dipped sharply after the Democrat midterm win (markets interpreted it as a possible brake on US military escalation) but have since partially recovered, with crude (WTI) sitting at around $90.83 a barrel. Sustained oil prices at this level add to inflation pressure globally and complicate interest rate decisions for central banks, including the RBA.

stories.title: US prosecutor leading Trump-backed election probe quits Justice Department
stories.why_it_matters: The special prosecutor who was leading a Trump-backed investigation into the 2024 presidential election has resigned from the Justice Department. The probe had been a politically charged saga, with Trump claiming he was targeted by the Biden administration during the election. The departure removes a key figure from an already contentious investigation, and comes at a moment when Trump's political authority is weakened by the midterm result.

markets.summary: Last night the NASDAQ jumped over 1% and the S&P 500 edged up, as markets digested the Democrat midterm win. The ASX fell 0.49% today, dragged by global uncertainty. Gold slipped, the Aussie dollar weakened, and oil is holding steady near $91.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: The ASX closed down nearly half a percent today, weighed down by global uncertainty following the US midterms and ongoing Iran conflict concerns.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: The S&P 500 edged up 0.31% last night — markets saw the Democrat win as potentially reducing the risk of further Middle East escalation.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: The NASDAQ gained over 1% last night. Tech stocks like Google recovered, though AI regulation concerns kept a lid on some names.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil is holding around $91 a barrel. Ship attacks in the Persian Gulf are keeping supply concerns alive, even as ceasefire talks for Iran continue.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold dropped nearly 1% last night — when equity markets rallied, some investors moved money out of safe-haven assets like gold.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar fell about 0.9 cents against the US dollar today. A weaker AUD makes your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) worth a little more in Aussie dollar terms when you convert back.

politics.summary: The US midterm result is sending shockwaves into Australian politics, with experts saying Albanese faces the same voter discontent that flipped Congress. The RBA has hiked rates again to 4.85%, and a Senate integrity saga is brewing around independent senator Fatima Payman.

stories.title: US midterm result should 'scare the heck out of Albanese', analysts say
stories.why_it_matters: Political experts are drawing direct parallels between the voter anger that handed Democrats a midterm win in the US and the pressures facing the Albanese Labor government. Issues like cost-of-living, housing affordability, and energy bills are cited as the common thread. With an Australian federal election on the horizon, the message is clear: incumbent governments are vulnerable when everyday people are struggling.

stories.title: RBA hikes cash rate to 4.85% — big four banks lift savings rates
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank has raised the official cash rate again, this time to 4.85%. CBA, NAB, Westpac and ANZ have all responded by lifting savings account rates — good news for savers, bad news for mortgage holders who will see repayments climb again. This is the latest in a series of hikes aimed at bringing inflation under control, but it's adding real financial pressure on Australian households.

stories.title: Senator Payman claims Albanese offered extra staff in exchange for her vote
stories.why_it_matters: Independent senator Fatima Payman has alleged that PM Albanese offered her additional parliamentary staff in exchange for her vote on a piece of legislation. If true, it raises serious questions about how the government secures crossbench support. Payman left the Labor party in 2024 over the Gaza conflict and has been a thorn in the government's side ever since. The claim adds to a picture of a minority government under pressure.

stories.title: Energy rebate blowout: taxpayers spent $5.5 billion on power bill relief
stories.why_it_matters: Australians received $5.5 billion in government energy bill rebates — but the cost to taxpayers has blown out well beyond initial projections. Critics argue the scheme was poorly targeted and expensive, while defenders say it was necessary relief during a cost-of-living crisis. Either way, it's a significant budget hit that will feature in the upcoming political debate about fiscal responsibility heading into the election.

stories.title: AUKUS Bill passes, hands sweeping powers to the Defence Minister
stories.why_it_matters: Parliament has passed AUKUS legislation giving the Defence Minister sweeping new powers to manage Australia's nuclear-powered submarine program. Critics say the powers are too broad and lack adequate oversight, while the government argues the program's complexity demands streamlined decision-making. AUKUS remains one of Australia's biggest strategic bets — a multi-decade, multi-hundred-billion-dollar commitment to US and UK defence partnership.

ai.summary: The Democrat midterm win has supercharged the AI regulation debate in Washington, triggering a sell-off in AI stocks. Meanwhile, OpenAI has quietly dropped GPT-6 Cyber — a new model aimed squarely at cybersecurity.

stories.title: Democrats plan flood of AI regulation bills after taking Congress
stories.why_it_matters: With Democrats now controlling Congress, Reuters reports they are preparing a wave of AI regulation bills covering everything from data privacy and algorithmic accountability to AI use in weapons systems. This is a sharp shift from the relatively hands-off approach under Republican leadership. For tech companies like Microsoft, Google, and the AI ETF you hold, more regulation means higher compliance costs and potentially slower AI product rollouts — which is why AI stocks sold off hard on the news.

stories.title: AI regulation fears wipe billions from tech valuations
stories.why_it_matters: Markets reacted sharply to the prospect of incoming AI regulation, with a multi-trillion dollar sell-off wiping billions from tech company valuations. AI-focused ETFs like your GXAI.AX bore the brunt. The key question analysts are debating: is this a temporary panic, or the start of a more structural re-rating of AI stocks? Most long-term observers say the AI growth story is intact — regulation adds friction but doesn't stop the train.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber to rival Claude and Gemini
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a specialised AI model built specifically for cybersecurity — designed to compete directly with Anthropic's Claude Mythos and Google's Gemini. What can it actually do? According to reports, it can find software vulnerabilities that human hackers could exploit, which OpenAI says will help defenders patch systems faster than attackers can use them. It's a double-edged sword — same tech that finds flaws can theoretically be used to attack them — which is exactly the kind of thing that will accelerate the AI regulation push in Congress.

stories.title: What would AI regulation actually look like in practice?
stories.why_it_matters: As the AI regulation debate heats up, analysts are asking: what would the rules actually look like? Early proposals include mandatory safety testing before AI products are deployed, liability laws if AI causes harm, transparency requirements (so users know when they're talking to AI), and restrictions on AI in weapons or critical infrastructure. AI companies are warning that heavy-handed rules could push development offshore to less regulated countries — a key argument they'll make to Congress.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done — Roosters beat the Knights 19-18 in a thriller. Big injury and signing news to get through, plus Kyrgios confirms he'll play on in 2027, and AFL draft season is hotting up.

stories.title: ROOSTERS 19 def. KNIGHTS 18 — NRL Grand Final thriller at Accor Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters won the 2026 NRL premiership by the skin of their teeth, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in what must have been a heart-stopper at Accor Stadium. One point in it at the final whistle. The grand final between Roosters and Knights set up a blockbuster clash — and it delivered.

stories.title: Casualty ward: Toia out with leg injury, Ponga returns for Knights
stories.why_it_matters: Knights prop Toia is ruled out of the grand final with a leg injury, while star fullback Kalyn Ponga has returned from his own injury lay-off to play. Ponga's presence will have been a massive boost for Newcastle in the decider, while losing Toia hurt their forward pack going into the biggest game of the year.

stories.title: Eels make huge call on Addo-Carr's future after drugs test twist
stories.why_it_matters: The Parramatta Eels have made a significant call on Josh Addo-Carr's future following a drugs test controversy. The article doesn't detail the specific decision, but a drugs test 'twist' suggests the situation has taken an unexpected turn — either clearing him or revealing new information. Addo-Carr has been one of the NRL's most dynamic wingers and his future has significant implications for Parramatta's 2027 squad.

stories.title: Nick Kyrgios confirms 2027 return — first tournament after difficult season
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has confirmed he'll play on in 2027, putting to rest retirement rumours that swirled after a difficult 2026 season that included a suspension and an emotional Wimbledon farewell. His first tournament of 2027 has been confirmed. For Australian tennis fans, it's good news — Kyrgios remains one of the most watchable players on tour when fit and motivated.

stories.title: Cleary rejects astonishing contract offer — NRL signing tracker update
stories.why_it_matters: Panthers halfback Nathan Cleary has reportedly knocked back an astonishing contract offer — described as a sum most players would never see in their careers. Jett (reported to be an overseas-based player) is flying home in the NRL signings tracker, and the Warriors have extended Tuaupiki. The off-season transfer market is in full swing ahead of 2027.
